title: Slow-Cooked Garlic Aglio e Olio
description: A refined take on aglio e olio built on garlic blanched four times to strip harshness and bitterness, then blended with EVOO and starchy pasta water into a completely smooth emulsion. No cream, no butter — just silky, sweet garlic.
equipment: carbon steel wok or large skillet

steps.title: Prep garlic

steps.title: Blanch garlic four times
steps.text: Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Add {i01} and boil for 1 minute. Strain and let the garlic rest for 1 minute. Repeat this boil-strain-rest cycle a total of 4 times. This removes harshness and bitterness, leaving a sweeter, smoother flavor.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.text: Bring a well-salted pot of water to a boil. Cook {i04} until al dente according to package directions. Before draining, reserve {i03} of the starchy pasta water. Set pasta aside.

steps.text: Transfer the hot cooked {i04} directly into the garlic emulsion — either in a pan over gentle heat or directly in the blender vessel if it's wide enough. Toss aggressively so the starch from the pasta water stabilizes the sauce and creates a glossy texture.

CAPTION (as written by the author -- trust these amounts):
🧄 100g GARLIC. ZERO CREAM. INSANE TEXTURE.

The secret to the creamiest Aglio e Olio?
Slow-cooked garlic. 🧄🔥

Cook the garlic gently until sweet, soft and silky, then emulsify with EVOO + starchy pasta water.

No cream. Just GARLIC. 🧄✨

1 Serving
🧄 Garlic 100g
🫒 EVOO 120g
💧 Pasta water 120g
🍝 Spaghetti 120g
🌿 Parsley
🌶️ Cayenne
🧂 Salt

Save this one. You’ll never look at Aglio e Olio the same way. 🍝

#aglioeolio #garlic #pasta #spaghetti #italianfood pastarecipe foodie michelin

SPOKEN TRANSCRIPT (what they say in the video -- the method is usually here, and often includes steps the caption omits):
Most alloy recipes are too aggressive, too heavy, and with too much raw garlic flavor, but this version is different. Peel the garlic and remove the germ inside. Then boil it in water for 1 minute. Strain it and let it rest for 1 minute more. Repeat this process 4 times. You lose the harshness and bitterness, leaving behind a sweeter, smoother flavor profile. Now blend the cooked garlic with olive oil and pasta water until completely silky. Now cook this baguette el dente and transfer them directly into the garlic emotion. Add freshly chopped parsley and toss aggressively. The starch from pasta water stabilizes the sauce and creates that glossy texture without cream or butter. Finish with cayenne pepper. The result is completely different from the classic home-style aloe oil. It's softer, more elegant and controlled.
